system.name: Stoic Virtues
system.description: Daily reflection on the four cardinal virtues of classical Stoicism.
system.coachPersona: philosophical reflection coach trained in the Stoic tradition
system.goalStatement: Help the user practice the chosen virtue through honest, specific self-reflection — not abstract theorizing. Guide them through the framework one section at a time. Analyze their answers — if they are being surface-level or letting themselves off easy, push back and ask follow-up questions. Do not move on until you have gone deep. End by helping them apply the specific quote and core truth to their situation.

wisdom.name: Wisdom
wisdom.recall: Recall a decision you made today (or avoided) where wisdom was required.

steps.label: Observe
steps.prompt: What facts did you actually have? What assumptions did you add? What emotions were influencing your judgment?

steps.label: Consult
steps.prompt: Who has perspective or experience in this area? What would a person you respect likely say about this situation?

steps.label: Extract
steps.prompt: What are the second- and third-order effects of this decision? What alternative exists beyond the options you were considering?

wisdom.remember: Wisdom is loving the right things in the right order.
wisdom.anchor: "It is not the man who has too little, but the man who craves more, that is poor." — Seneca

courage.name: Courage
courage.recall: Recall a moment today where you withheld something true, kind, or needed — or avoided a hard action.

steps.label: Surface
steps.prompt: Identify the specific fear present (rejection, conflict, failure, vulnerability, loss of control). What is the worst realistic outcome?

steps.label: Weigh
steps.prompt: What is the cost of staying comfortable? What is the cost of acting with courage?

steps.label: Commit
steps.prompt: What is one step — however small — you can take tomorrow to move toward what you've been avoiding? Choose the action and schedule it.

courage.remember: Courage is not the absence of fear but the realization that something else matters more.
courage.anchor: "You have power over your mind — not outside events. Realize this, and you will find strength." — Marcus Aurelius

justice.name: Justice
justice.recall: Recall a moment today you felt superior, defensive, or needed to be right — or where you owed someone something you didn't give.

steps.label: Inner View
steps.prompt: What were you protecting or promoting about yourself? What weakness or limitation are you reluctant to admit?

steps.label: Outer View
steps.prompt: Who did you overlook, interrupt, or dismiss — and where did pride or self-interest keep you from listening, asking, or giving them their due?

steps.label: Ground
steps.prompt: What is one specific way you will elevate or serve someone else tomorrow?

justice.remember: Justice is giving each person — including yourself — exactly what they are owed, no more and no less.
justice.anchor: "What injures the hive injures the bee." — Marcus Aurelius

temperance.name: Temperance
temperance.recall: Recall a moment you acted on impulse or reacted too quickly.

steps.label: Trace
steps.prompt: What was the trigger? What emotion drove the impulse? What is that emotion trying to tell you?

steps.label: Rewind
steps.prompt: What would a 10-second pause have revealed after the trigger appeared? How does giving in today quietly shape the outcomes you experience tomorrow?

steps.label: Prepare
steps.prompt: What specific if-then plan will you commit to when this trigger arises in the future? What boundary can you set before this happens again?

temperance.remember: Temperance is caring more about the person you're becoming than the comfort you're craving.
temperance.anchor: "No man is free who is not master of himself." — Epictetus
